From 6f52370970ac07d352a7af4089e55e0e6425f827 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Anil Samal <anil.samal@intel.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2026 13:39:45 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] RDMA/irdma: Fix deadlock during netdev reset with active
 connections

Resolve deadlock that occurs when user executes netdev reset while RDMA
applications (e.g., rping) are active. The netdev reset causes ice
driver to remove irdma auxiliary driver, triggering device_delete and
subsequent client removal. During client removal, uverbs_client waits
for QP reference count to reach zero while cma_client holds the final
reference, creating circular dependency and indefinite wait in iWARP
mode. Skip QP reference count wait during device reset to prevent
deadlock.

Fixes: c8f304d75f6c ("RDMA/irdma: Prevent QP use after free")
Signed-off-by: Anil Samal <anil.samal@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Tatyana Nikolova <tatyana.e.nikolova@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/infiniband/hw/irdma/verbs.c b/drivers/infiniband/hw/irdma/verbs.c
index 9920a3304be3..95f590c10c05 100644
--- a/drivers/infiniband/hw/irdma/verbs.c
+++ b/drivers/infiniband/hw/irdma/verbs.c
@@ -558,7 +558,8 @@ static int irdma_destroy_qp(struct ib_qp *ibqp, struct ib_udata *udata)
 	}
 
 	irdma_qp_rem_ref(&iwqp->ibqp);
-	wait_for_completion(&iwqp->free_qp);
+	if (!iwdev->rf->reset)
+		wait_for_completion(&iwqp->free_qp);
 	irdma_free_lsmm_rsrc(iwqp);
 	irdma_cqp_qp_destroy_cmd(&iwdev->rf->sc_dev, &iwqp->sc_qp);
 
-- 
2.34.1

This patch fixes a deadlock in the Intel irdma RDMA driver by conditionally skipping a wait operation during device reset when RDMA connections are active.

### Modifications in each file

**`drivers/infiniband/hw/irdma/verbs.c`**:
- In function `irdma_destroy_qp`, the unconditional call to `wait_for_completion(&iwqp->free_qp)` is now guarded by a check of the `reset` flag (`if (!iwdev->rf->reset)`).
- When the device is being reset, the driver no longer waits for the QP reference count to drop to zero, thus breaking the circular dependency that caused the deadlock.

### Relationships between modifications

The change is contained within a single function of one file. The relationship is between the condition and the blocked wait:
- The original code always waited for the QP to be freed, which under reset scenarios caused deadlock because the final reference was held by the `cma_client` while `uverbs_client` waited indefinitely.
- Adding the `reset` flag check ensures that the wait is bypassed only when a device reset is in progress, allowing the teardown to proceed without waiting for the QP reference count to reach zero. This resolves the deadlock while preserving normal wait behavior during non-reset operations.

Root cause:
uverbs_client waits for QP reference count to reach zero in irdma_destroy_qp, while cma_client holds the final reference, causing an indefinite wait.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
wait_for_completion(&iwqp->free_qp);
Reason:
This line unconditionally waits for the completion of QP reference count reaching zero. During netdev reset, uverbs_client calls irdma_destroy_qp and waits indefinitely because cma_client holds the final reference and cannot release it due to the reset sequence, causing a deadlock.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (!iwdev->rf->reset)
	wait_for_completion(&iwqp->free_qp);
Reason:
By skipping the wait when a device reset is in progress (checked via iwdev->rf->reset), the deadlock is avoided. During reset, the reference count will be cleaned up later, so waiting is unnecessary and harmful. The conditional ensures that the normal path still waits for QP destruction when no reset is occurring.
